text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- Interior Minister Vidmantas Ziemelis signed an order severely reprimanding a Kaunas police inspector for leaking information to the press.
- Lithuania will prepare a 400-page official comment on the European Commission's evaluation of Lithuania by the middle of August to present to European Union member states.
- Estonian President Lenart Meri will make an official visit to Lithuania on August 20-22.
- Largest caramel confectionary, Naujoji Ruta, had turnover of 25 million litas in the first half of 1997.
- The central bank applied to the foreign ministry and the Russian central bank to clarify the situation surrounding the freezing of correspondent accounts of four Lithuanian banks.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- Snoras Bank had 472,000 litas in the correspondent account that was frozen in Russia for allegedly not paying value added taxes.
- The government decided on July 30 to tax income on money transferred to tax havens abroad by 29 percent, affecting retroactively money that was transferred as of July 1.
- Inflation in July was 1.1 percent compared to a previously projected 0.2 percent due to higher prices for hot water, electricity, gas and other fuels.
- The reserves of the central bank increased to $1.153 billion at the end of July from $939.6 million one month before.
- The agriculture ministry plans to increase milk subsidies to 57-58 litas per tonne from 54 litas per tonne.
- The finance ministry picked J.P. Morgan to arrange a 3-year $100 million syndicated loan at LIBOR plus 0.45.
- Brewer Kalnapilis passed Utena beverages to gain the top spot among Lithuanian brewers in terms of sales. Utena was second and Shvyturys was third.
- The economy ministry will prepare a privatisation programme for the Mazeikiu Nafta oil refinery by August 28.
RESPUBLIKA
- Organisers of the September 5-6 conference of seven east European heads of state and the Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin say they expect 100 participants and 300 journalists.
LIETUVOS AIDAS

- The Lithuanian National Socialist Unity Alliance, based in Siauliai, said it will not alter its publications despite a reprimand from the state security department saying the organisation was promoting racism.
-- Burton Frierson, Vilnius newsroom + 370 2 22 35 18
